items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Lloyd paid me and the rest of the musicians $17.00 for our part... I never thought that Lloyd had cheated me out of anything if he took a bigger cut from the percentage because he had the responsibility of transportation and other things.

ctx.x: What had happened was that Broadus had stopped in a small town to have some sort of cold drink because he was tired of driving and wanted to rest for a while also. He had not put the brakes on tight enough and the car had rolled backwards down a hill. Fortunately, the musicians that sat in front had not gone with Broadus but were standing on the side of the road and saw the car when it started to roll down this hill and they managed to get two big rocks under both back wheels and stop the car about 5 feet from a…

In Lexington I stayed with Henry Jamerson and his mother. Jamerson had been with an organisation known as Musical Spiller when he was very young. He told me that Spiller had a musical act made of members of his family and other talented young musicians that he discovered, and arranged with the families of these young musicians to let them travel with him. Therefore Musical Spiller had a musical act. Jamerson travelled quite extensively with Spiller and then joined the orchestra of Lloyd Scott who was from…
Jamerson had left the Scott orchestra because his mother's health was not very good and she was alone. He was the only child and he decided to stay at home with his mother until she passed away.
